title: Affine representability of pushouts of commutative group extensions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $0\to N\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{q}Q\to0$ be an exact sequence of commutative affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where $i$ is a closed subgroup embedding [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] identifying $N$ with the scheme-theoretic kernel, and $q$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Let $\varphi:N\to\mathbf G_a$ be a group homomorphism [def-sc-gm-ga]. Define $J\subseteq B\times\mathbf G_a$ by the closed embedding $n\mapsto(i(n),-\varphi(n))$. The fppf sheafification of $R\mapsto(B(R)\times R)/J(R)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras is represented by a commutative affine finite-type $k$-group scheme $E$. The quotient map $\rho:B\times\mathbf G_a\to E$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. Put $b(x)=\rho(x,0)$, $j(t)=\rho(0,t)$, and let $q':E\to Q$ be induced by $(x,t)\mapsto q(x)$. Then $0\to\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q'}Q\to0$ is exact in the same sense, $bi=j\varphi$, $q'b=q$, and this square is a pushout in represented fppf sheaves of commutative groups. Products are over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Proposition 5.18 (affine quotient by a normal algebraic subgroup), printed pp.102-103; Theorem 5.13, printed pp.100-101, for the quotient universal property; the pushout diagram in the proof of Proposition 14.48, printed p.296. The displayed antidiagonal quotient is the explicit pushout used there.

proof.text: Put $G=B\times\mathbf G_a$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies its coordinate ring with $k[B][T]$, so $G$ is affine of finite type. The map $a:N\to G$, $n\mapsto(i(n),-\varphi(n))$, is a homomorphism since the groups are commutative. Its coordinate map $k[B][T]\to k[N]$ extends the surjection $i^*:k[B]\to k[N]$ and sends $T$ to $-\varphi^*(T)$; it is therefore surjective. Thus $a$ is a closed immersion by the affine criterion (Stacks Tag 01QO). Its image $J\simeq N$ is a finite-type normal subgroup of $G$: on every algebra the image is a subgroup, and $G(R)$ is abelian.

source.place: Proposition 5.18, printed p.103; antidiagonal construction making explicit Proposition 14.48, printed p.296

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to $J\subseteq G$. It gives an affine finite-type group scheme $E=G/J$ representing exactly the fppf sheafification in the statement, with quotient $\rho:G\to E$ faithfully flat and finitely presented and scheme-theoretic kernel $J$. Its sheaf sections lift locally to $G$. Two local lifts commute because $G$ is commutative, hence the multiplication of $E$ is commutative as well; equality descends since $E$ is a sheaf. Define $b(x)=\rho(x,0)$ and $j(t)=\rho(0,t)$.

source.place: Proposition 5.18, printed p.103; quotient/sheaf interpretation in Section 5(j), printed pp.116–118

proof.text: The homomorphism $q\operatorname{pr}_B:G\to Q$ vanishes on $J$, since $qi=0$. The quotient universal property [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal], applied to $\rho$ with target $Q$, produces a unique homomorphism $q':E\to Q$ satisfying $q'\rho=q\operatorname{pr}_B$. In particular $q'b=q$ and $q'j=0$. For every algebra and $n\in N(R)$, the relation $\rho(i(n),-\varphi(n))=0$ gives $b(i(n))=j(\varphi(n))$, so $bi=j\varphi$ as group-scheme morphisms.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101; Proposition 14.48 pushout diagram, printed p.296

proof.text: Let $K=\ker(q')$, a closed subgroup of $E$ by [lem-sc-kernel-subgroup]; hence it is affine of finite type (its coordinate algebra is a quotient of $k[E]$). For every $R$, if $j(t)=0$, the equality $\ker(\rho)(R)=J(R)$ supplies $n\in N(R)$ with $(0,t)=(i(n),-\varphi(n))$. Injectivity of $i(R)$ gives $n=0$, then $t=0$. Thus $j$ is injective on every algebra. If $e\in K(R)$, lift it fppf locally through $\rho$ to $(x,t)$. Then $q(x)=0$, so uniquely $x=i(n)$; the relation gives $e=j(t+\varphi(n))$. These local values of $t+\varphi(n)$ agree on overlaps by the just-proved injectivity and glue uniquely by representable descent [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Thus $\mathbf G_a(R)\to K(R)$ is bijective naturally in $R$. Yoneda on affine schemes makes $j:\mathbf G_a\to K$ an isomorphism. In particular $j:\mathbf G_a\to E$ is the closed kernel embedding, not merely injective on field points.

source.place: Proposition 14.48, printed p.296, exact pushout row; Stacks Tag 023Q (descent-lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms) for gluing the unique additive coordinate

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] to the closed normal subgroup $K\subseteq E$, obtaining $p:E\to D=E/K$, faithfully flat and finitely presented. All $B,Q,E,D$ are affine of finite type. The map $pb:B\to D$ kills $N$ since $bi=j\varphi$, and $q'$ kills $K$. Apply [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] to $q$ and $p$ respectively to obtain $u:Q\to D$, $v:D\to Q$ with $uq=pb$, $vp=q'$. Now $vuq=q'b=q$, so uniqueness for $q$ gives $vu=1_Q$. Also $uvp\rho=uq\operatorname{pr}_B=pb\operatorname{pr}_B=p\rho$: indeed $\rho(x,t)=b(x)+j(t)$ and $pj=0$. Uniqueness for $\rho$ and then $p$ gives $uv=1_D$. Consequently $v$ is an isomorphism and $q'=vp$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, with kernel identified in step 4. This proves the asserted exactness in the original scheme-theoretic sense.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101, and Proposition 5.18, printed p.103; exact pushout row of Proposition 14.48, printed p.296

proof.text: For any fppf sheaf $H$ of commutative groups and homomorphisms $f:B\to H$, $g:\mathbf G_a\to H$ with $fi=g\varphi$, the homomorphism $(x,t)\mapsto f(x)+g(t)$ kills $J$: on $a(n)$ its value is $fi(n)-g\varphi(n)=0$. It therefore gives a natural homomorphism from the orbit presheaf $R\mapsto G(R)/J(R)$ to $H$. The universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives a unique sheaf homomorphism $h:E\to H$ with $h\rho(x,t)=f(x)+g(t)$, so $hb=f$ and $hj=g$. Conversely every such $h$ must satisfy this formula, which proves uniqueness. This is the pushout property even among all commutative fppf sheaves, hence among represented ones.
